text:
Marta: FYI after yesterday's demo we got a short burst where the gateway waited on admission and served 503s. Thinking we should separate fast-path decisions from longer admission reconciliation.
Liam: Any quick traces? was the gateway waiting on token checkout or a lease reconcile? :thinking:
Marta: tail from logs:
```
2026-02-12T18:03:41Z ingress-gw INFO req=abcd token_check=ok route=/v1/generate latency=12ms
2026-02-12T18:03:42Z ingress-gw WARN req=abce hold=admission delay=850ms
2026-02-12T18:03:42Z admission-svc ERR req=abce err=lease_reconcile timeout=5000ms
2026-02-12T18:03:42Z ingress-gw ERR req=abce respond=503
```
Marta: Looks like gw blocked on admission decision and then returned 503. We should avoid gw blocking on long-tail admission work.
Devon: Two approaches I'd consider:
- Gateway early-fail: if admission not ready, fail quickly (good for keeping p99 low)
- Provisional admission: gw accepts provisional permits with short TTL and lower priority while admission reconciles in background
Each has fairness/abuse tradeoffs.
Sam: Provisional tokens worry me: accounting, abuse signals, and later revokes. How do we handle eviction and refunds?
Marta: Sketch: admission returns an AdmissionDecision with states GRANT / PROVISIONAL / REJECT and fields lease_id, provisional_ttl_ms, degrade_target. Gateway treats PROVISIONAL as allowed but tagged and lower-priority.
Liam: proto draft:
```
message AdmissionDecision {
  enum State { GRANT = 0; PROVISIONAL = 1; REJECT = 2; }
  State state = 1;
  string lease_id = 2;
  int32 provisional_ttl_ms = 3;
  string degrade_to = 4; // fallback model/handler
}
```
Devon: With provisional we avoid blocking but admission must eventually reconcile and either confirm or revoke. That implies a reconciliation pipeline and chargeback reconciliation runs.
Sam: Key questions:
- When do we bill? immediately or after reconcile?
- If revoked, do we refund or mark as overage?
- How to make reconcilers idempotent and observable?
Marta: Tradeoffs: provisional reduces latency SLO violations but increases complexity (reconcile, refunds, counters). Fast-fail reduces complexity but may increase client retries and visible failures.
Liam: My suggestion: start conservative. Enable provisional only for low-cost, low-abuse routes (embeddings, short-run generates). Keep high-cost gen routes fast-fail for now.
Devon: Also add an in-gateway short-lived admission cache keyed by tenant+route (TTL ~ 500-1000ms) to avoid thundering herd toward admission for hot keys.
Sam: Telemetry we should capture up-front: provisional_allowed_count, provisional_revoked_count, provisional_duration_ms_histogram, reconcile_refunds_total, per-route p50/p95/p99 with provisional tag. Tag by tenant and priority.
Marta: Ops checklist for an experiment:
- Proto + AdmissionDecision enum (Marta)
- Gateway cache guard and provisional flow (Devon)
- Reconciliation worker + refund/accounting batch (Sam)
- Telemetry metrics + dashboards and alert runbook (Liam)
- Canary plan: staging smoke -> 2% prod for 48h -> ramp (Marta)
Liam: I'll open a telemetry PR with metric names and alert thresholds.
Devon: I'll draft cache semantics and note interactions with admission leader election.
Sam: I'll write reconcile failure modes and a refund policy (soft refund vs hard bill).
Marta: One last policy decision: charge on issuance then reconcile refund if revoked (keeps billing consistent). Thoughts?
Sam: Charge-on-issue reduces accounting complexity and discourages abuse. Refunds must be auditable and rate-limited.
Liam: Sounds reasonable. I'll take this into an RFC + canary playbook and link the telemetry PR.
Devon: Also add a small simulator harness for bursty clients to validate fairness heuristics before canary.
Marta: Great. I'll open the RFC and assign owners. Will follow up with a mini spike test. :thumbsup:
